countries.name: Antigua and Barbuda
countries.summary: Antigua is one of the drier, sunnier islands in the eastern Caribbean, famous for its 365 beaches and its sailing. The dry season from mid-December to April is the best and busiest time, ending with the Classic Yacht Regatta and Antigua Sailing Week in late April and early May. May to July is good value, with Carnival from late July to early August. The hurricane season (June to November) peaks from mid-August to October; Irma (2017) destroyed most of Barbuda.
countries.splitReason: Two low, dry islands with one tropical climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: St. John's, English Harbour and Nelson's Dockyard, the beaches of Dickenson Bay, Jolly Harbour and Half Moon Bay, and Barbuda.

best.why: Dry, sunny 28–29 °C days and steady trade winds, ending with the Classic Yacht Regatta and Sailing Week.

worst.why: Hurricane peak, with the wettest weather of the year; many hotels close in September–October.

shoulder.why: Dry and sunny but festive peak prices.
Warm and good value; Carnival in late July and early August, but sargassum on east-facing beaches.
Rains easing; low prices before the season.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Irma (2017) destroyed most buildings on Barbuda.
Seaweed can pile up on the Atlantic-facing east coast (Half Moon Bay, Long Bay).

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak rates and minimum stays at the resorts; English Harbour is full of superyachts.

recurringHolidays.name: Antigua Sailing Week
recurringHolidays.effect: One of the Caribbean's biggest regattas; English Harbour and Falmouth accommodation books out.

recurringHolidays.name: Antigua Carnival
recurringHolidays.approx: Late July – first Tuesday of August
recurringHolidays.effect: Calypso, soca and the J'ouvert parade in St. John's.

prices.notes: Mostly all-inclusive and upscale; apartments around Jolly Harbour and English Harbour are cheaper. Barbuda is a day trip by ferry or small plane.

countries.name: Aruba
countries.summary: Aruba lies off Venezuela, outside the hurricane belt, and is dry, sunny and breezy all year (29–32 °C, about 450 mm of rain). There is no bad time to visit: the winter high season (mid-December to April) is about escaping the northern winter and has the highest prices, while summer is hotter, windier and cheaper, with steady trade winds that make it a kitesurfing and windsurfing hotspot. The short rainy season from October to December brings only brief showers. Carnival before Lent and the US holidays are the busiest times.
countries.splitReason: A small, flat, arid island with one climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Oranjestad, Palm Beach and Eagle Beach, Arashi and the California Lighthouse, Arikok National Park and San Nicolas with Baby Beach.

best.why: Dry, sunny 29 °C days and a cooling breeze while the north is in winter; Carnival season.
The driest, sunniest months with strong trade winds for kitesurfing, and prices well below winter.

shoulder.why: The short rainy season (brief showers, calmer winds), then Christmas peak prices.

risks.note: Trade winds of 25–30 km/h; great for kitesurfing, choppy for snorkelling.
Aruba lies south of the hurricane belt and direct hits are very rare.

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival
recurringHolidays.approx: The weeks before Lent; Grand Parade on the Sunday before Ash Wednesday
recurringHolidays.effect: Night parades in Oranjestad and San Nicolas; hotels fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Soul Beach Music Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: A big music festival; Palm Beach hotels book out.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Palm Beach and Eagle Beach resorts are at peak rates; book months ahead.

prices.notes: Prices are in US dollars, and Aruba is one of the costlier Caribbean islands. Supermarkets and apartments help cut costs.

countries.name: Barbados
countries.summary: Barbados is the most easterly Caribbean island and is breezy and 29–31 °C all year. The dry season from mid-December to April brings sunshine and calm west-coast seas, but also the highest prices. The rainy season runs from June to November, peaking in September to November, and although Barbados lies on the eastern edge of the hurricane belt, direct hits are rare. Summer belongs to Crop Over, the island's carnival, which climaxes with Grand Kadooment in early August.
countries.splitReason: A small island with one tropical climate; the east (Atlantic) coast is windier and rougher than the calm west.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Bridgetown, the west-coast Platinum Coast (Holetown, Speightstown), the south coast (Oistins, St Lawrence Gap) and the wild east coast at Bathsheba.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 29 °C days, steady trade winds and calm, clear water on the west coast.

worst.why: Wettest, most humid weeks and peak hurricane season, with tropical storms and choppy seas.

shoulder.why: Dry and sunny but festive peak prices and minimum stays.
Warm and good value as the rains begin; sargassum can affect south and east beaches.
Crop Over season: lively and showery, with festival price rises.
Still showery, but prices are low before the winter season.

risks.note: Barbados lies on the eastern edge of the belt; direct hits are rare, but storms pass close by (Beryl 2024).
Seaweed piles up on the south and east coasts in some years.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Platinum Coast villas and hotels charge peak rates, often with minimum stays.

recurringHolidays.name: Crop Over
recurringHolidays.effect: The island's carnival: fetes, calypso tents and the Grand Kadooment road march; flights and hotels fill.

prices.notes: The west coast is expensive; the south coast (St Lawrence Gap, Dover) has cheaper apartments. Oistins' Friday fish fry is a cheap night out.

countries.name: Bermuda
countries.summary: Bermuda is in the subtropical Atlantic, about 1,000 km east of North Carolina, not the Caribbean, so its seasons are very different. May to October is the warm season, with 25–30 °C days and a sea warm enough for the pink-sand beaches, peaking around Cup Match at the end of July. Hurricanes pass close by most often from August to October (Fabian 2003, Gonzalo 2014, Ernesto 2024). Winters are mild but windy and grey, with 20 °C days and a sea too cool for most swimmers, making it the quiet low season.
countries.splitReason: A small group of islands with one subtropical oceanic climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Hamilton, the Town of St. George, the South Shore beaches (Horseshoe Bay, Warwick Long Bay, Elbow Beach) and the Royal Naval Dockyard.

best.why: Warm 24–30 °C days and a 22–28 °C sea for the pink-sand beaches, snorkelling and wreck diving.

worst.why: Mild but windy and grey, at 20 °C with a 19 °C sea; too cool for beach days.

shoulder.why: Spring warmth, Good Friday kites and quiet golf courses, but the sea is still cool.
A warm sea and fewer crowds, but the hurricane peak (September).
Cooler, breezy and cheap; good for golf and walking.

risks.note: Storms pass close to Bermuda most often from August to October; buildings are hurricane-proof but flights are cancelled.
Winter gales bring rough seas and cancelled ferry sailings.

recurringHolidays.name: Good Friday kite flying
recurringHolidays.effect: Islanders fly home-made kites at Horseshoe Bay and across the island; a public holiday.

recurringHolidays.name: Bermuda Day
recurringHolidays.effect: A parade in Hamilton and the traditional first swim of the year.

recurringHolidays.name: Cup Match
recurringHolidays.approx: Thursday and Friday before the first Monday in August
recurringHolidays.effect: Bermuda's biggest holiday: a two-day cricket match, beach parties and full ferries.

prices.notes: Very expensive: there are no hire cars, so visitors use buses, ferries and rented electric minicars. Guesthouses and winter deals are the cheapest options.

countries.name: Cayman Islands
countries.summary: The Cayman Islands are a British Overseas Territory famous for Seven Mile Beach and world-class wall diving. The dry season from December to April is sunny and 29 °C with calm seas, and is the high season. May to October is hotter and wetter, and the hurricane season peaks from mid-August to October (Ivan devastated Grand Cayman in 2004). Diving is excellent all year, with the calmest water in summer.
countries.splitReason: Three low, flat islands with one tropical climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Grand Cayman (George Town, Seven Mile Beach, West Bay, Stingray City, Rum Point), Cayman Brac and Little Cayman.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 29 °C days, low humidity and calm, clear water off Seven Mile Beach.

worst.why: Hurricane peak and the wettest months; some dive operators and resorts close in September.

shoulder.why: Hotter, with afternoon showers, but the calmest seas for diving and lower prices.
Rains easing, Pirates Week, then Christmas peak prices.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Ivan (2004) flooded much of Grand Cayman.
Occasional 'Nor'westers' (winter cold fronts) churn up Seven Mile Beach.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Seven Mile Beach resorts at peak rates with minimum stays.

recurringHolidays.name: Cayman Cookout
recurringHolidays.effect: A celebrity-chef food festival at Seven Mile Beach; the big resorts fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Batabano
recurringHolidays.effect: The Cayman carnival, with a road parade along West Bay Road.

recurringHolidays.name: Pirates Week
recurringHolidays.effect: A festival with costumes, parades and fireworks in George Town.

prices.notes: Among the most expensive places in the Caribbean, with prices in Cayman dollars (US dollars accepted everywhere). Condos and dive packages on Cayman Brac and Little Cayman are better value.

countries.name: Cuba
countries.summary: Cuba's dry season runs from December to April, when Havana, Viñales and Trinidad are sunny and 26–28 °C and the beaches of Varadero and the cays are at their best. May to October is hot and humid with heavy afternoon downpours, and the hurricane season (June to November) peaks from mid-August to October. The east (Santiago de Cuba, Baracoa, Holguín) is a couple of degrees hotter all year and Baracoa is the wettest corner of the island, with rain even in winter. Long power cuts and fuel and food shortages have hit the island since 2024, so check government travel advice before booking.

regions.name: Havana & western-central Cuba
regions.description: Havana, Viñales and Pinar del Río, Varadero, the Bay of Pigs, Cienfuegos, Trinidad, Santa Clara and the northern cays (Cayo Santa María, Cayo Coco).

best.why: Dry season: sunny 26–28 °C days, low humidity and calm seas, ideal for Havana's streets, the Viñales valley and Varadero.

worst.why: Hurricane-season peak and the wettest weeks (October is Havana's rainiest month), with heavy downpours, 32 °C humid heat and some hotels closed.

shoulder.why: Hot and increasingly humid; afternoon storms from late May, but low prices outside the July–August Cuban holidays.
Very hot and humid, with the hurricane season building.
Rains easing and temperatures dropping, though late-season storms are still possible.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; western Cuba was hit by Ian (2022) and Rafael (2024).
Tropical downpours that flood Havana's streets for an hour or two.

recurringHolidays.name: Havana International Jazz Festival (Jazz Plaza)
recurringHolidays.effect: Concerts across Havana; hotels and casas in Vedado fill up.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Canadian and European holidaymakers fill Varadero and the cays, and casas particulares in Havana and Trinidad book out.

recurringHolidays.name: Cuban summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Cuban families fill Varadero and the beach hotels; domestic buses and flights are full.

prices.notes: Casas particulares (private rooms) cost $30–60 a night and are better value than state hotels. Bring cash in euros or US dollars, as many foreign cards (all US-issued ones) don't work and ATMs are unreliable.

regions.name: Santiago de Cuba & the east
regions.description: Santiago de Cuba, the Sierra Maestra and Pico Turquino, Bayamo, Holguín and the Guardalavaca beaches, and Baracoa with Humboldt National Park.

best.why: Driest, sunniest months: 30 °C days in Santiago, Guardalavaca's beaches at their calmest and Baracoa's winter rains easing off.

worst.why: Hurricane peak and the wettest season: October downpours, and Baracoa and Santiago have taken direct hits (Matthew 2016, Sandy 2012).

shoulder.why: Dry and pleasant in Santiago and Holguín, but Baracoa is at its wettest and Christmas brings crowds.
Hot (33 °C) with May rains, but July brings Santiago's Carnival, the best in Cuba.
Sweltering heat and humidity as the hurricane season builds.

risks.note: The east is the most exposed part of Cuba; peak risk is late August to October.
Santiago is Cuba's hottest city, with humid 33–35 °C afternoons.
Heavy rain blocks La Farola, the mountain road into Baracoa.

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival of Santiago de Cuba
recurringHolidays.effect: Cuba's biggest carnival: congas and comparsas fill the streets and casas book out.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Canadian and European holidaymakers fill Varadero and the cays, and casas particulares in Havana and Trinidad book out.

recurringHolidays.name: Cuban summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Cuban families fill Varadero and the beach hotels; domestic buses and flights are full.

prices.notes: Cheaper than Havana. Long-distance Víazul buses are slow and fill up, so many travellers fly to Santiago or Holguín or hire a car with driver.

countries.name: Curaçao
countries.summary: Curaçao lies outside the hurricane belt, off the Venezuelan coast, and is dry and breezy at 29–32 °C all year. January to mid-April is the high season, with Carnival in the weeks before Lent. From mid-April to September the island is at its driest, and the trade winds ease from August to October to give the calmest, clearest water for diving and snorkelling the west-coast reefs; Dutch summer holidays fill rental villas in July and August. The short rainy season from October to December brings brief showers, not washouts.
countries.splitReason: A small, arid island with one climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Willemstad (Punda, Otrobanda, Pietermaai), the south-coast beaches (Jan Thiel, Mambo Beach), Westpunt and the coves of the west coast, Christoffel and Shete Boka national parks, and Klein Curaçao.

best.why: Dry, breezy 29–30 °C days and the Carnival season; the winter high season.
The driest months; from August the winds ease and the west-coast reefs are at their calmest and clearest for diving.

shoulder.why: The short rainy season with brief showers and calm seas, then Christmas peak prices.

risks.note: Curaçao is south of the hurricane belt; passing storms occasionally bring heavy rain.

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival
recurringHolidays.approx: The weeks before Lent; Grand March on the Sunday before Ash Wednesday
recurringHolidays.effect: Parades in Willemstad; hotels fill and roads close.

recurringHolidays.name: Dutch summer holidays
recurringHolidays.effect: Dutch families fill villas and apartments; flights from Amsterdam are at peak prices.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Fireworks and festivities in Willemstad; peak prices for flights and hotels.

prices.notes: Better value than Aruba, with apartments and dive resorts. A hire car is the easiest way to reach the western beaches.

countries.name: Dominica
countries.summary: Dominica, the 'Nature Isle', is mountainous, rainforested and one of the wettest islands in the Caribbean, with black-sand beaches rather than white ones. February to May is the driest time and the best for hiking the Waitukubuli Trail and the Boiling Lake, diving Champagne Reef and spotting the resident sperm whales. Rain is heavy from June to November, and the hurricane season peaks from mid-August to October; Maria (2017) devastated the island. The World Creole Music Festival in late October and Independence on 3 November bring a lively end to the rainy season.
countries.splitReason: A small island with one tropical calendar; the mountainous interior gets far more rain than the west coast around Roseau.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Roseau, Morne Trois Pitons and the Boiling Lake, Trafalgar Falls, Champagne Reef and Scotts Head, Portsmouth and the Indian River, Calibishie and the Kalinago Territory.

best.why: The driest months: firmer trails for the Boiling Lake and Waitukubuli Trail, calm seas and sperm whales off the west coast.

worst.why: Hurricane peak and torrential rain, with flooding, landslides and closed trails.

shoulder.why: Showery but green and quiet; whale-watching season is under way.
Rain increasing, humid and hot; trails get muddy.
Still wet, but the World Creole Music Festival and Independence celebrations liven things up.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Erika (2015) and Maria (2017) caused catastrophic floods and damage.
Heavy rain causes landslides and washes out roads and trail bridges.
Rivers rise fast after downpours; avoid river crossings on the trails.

recurringHolidays.name: Mas Domnik (Carnival)
recurringHolidays.approx: The Monday and Tuesday before Ash Wednesday
recurringHolidays.effect: Street parades and J'ouvert in Roseau; guesthouses fill.

recurringHolidays.name: World Creole Music Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: Three nights of Creole music in Roseau; rooms book out months ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: Independence & Creole Day
recurringHolidays.effect: National dress, Creole food and celebrations across the island.

prices.notes: Small eco-lodges and guesthouses ($80–150) rather than big resorts. Roads are steep and winding, so a hired car with a local guide for hikes is the norm.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
countries.summary: The Dominican Republic is warm all year (28–31 °C), and the dry season from December to April is the classic time to go: sunny, less humid, and from mid-January to March humpback whales gather in Samaná Bay. May is wet, and the hurricane season (June to November) peaks from mid-August to October. Summer is hot and showery but good value, though sargassum can reach the Punta Cana coast. Semana Santa and Christmas bring Dominican crowds and peak prices.
countries.splitReason: The beach areas share one Caribbean calendar; the central mountains (Jarabacoa, Constanza) are cooler but follow the same wet and dry seasons.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Punta Cana and Bávaro, La Romana and Bayahibe, Santo Domingo, Samaná and Las Terrenas, Puerto Plata, Sosúa and Cabarete, and the mountains around Jarabacoa.

best.why: Dry, sunny 28 °C days and calm seas; humpback whales calve in Samaná Bay from mid-January to March.

worst.why: Hurricane peak, the heaviest rain and sticky 31 °C heat; storm and flood risk is highest.

shoulder.why: Dry and sunny, but Christmas and New Year bring peak prices and full resorts.
May is the wettest spring month, but prices drop and June is good kitesurfing in Cabarete.
Hot, humid and showery; summer family crowds and sargassum on some eastern beaches.
The rains are easing and prices are still low.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; the east and south coasts are most exposed.
Seaweed can pile up on the Punta Cana and Bávaro beaches; resorts clear it daily.
Spring rains bring heavy afternoon downpours.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Resorts in Punta Cana and La Romana are at peak prices and Dominican families travel home.

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Parades in La Vega and Santo Domingo, ending around Independence Day (27 February).

recurringHolidays.name: Semana Santa
recurringHolidays.effect: Dominicans head to the beaches and rivers; resorts and roads are packed.

prices.notes: All-inclusive resorts dominate Punta Cana and can be excellent value outside the peak. Independent travel in Santo Domingo, Las Terrenas and Cabarete is cheaper.

countries.name: Grenada
countries.summary: Grenada, the 'Spice Isle', is 30–31 °C all year and lies near the southern edge of the hurricane belt. The dry season from January to May is the best time for Grand Anse beach, rainforest hikes and diving the underwater sculpture park. The rainy season runs from June to December with short, heavy showers, and the hurricane risk is lower than further north, though Ivan (2004) and Beryl (2024, which devastated Carriacou) show it is real. Spicemas, the island's carnival, peaks in the second week of August.
countries.splitReason: A small island with one tropical climate; the interior around Grand Etang is wetter and cooler.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: St. George's, Grand Anse and the south-west beaches, Grand Etang rainforest, Gouyave and Grenville, and the islands of Carriacou and Petite Martinique.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 30 °C days, calm seas for diving and dry trails in Grand Etang.

worst.why: The wettest weeks and the peak of the hurricane season, with heavy showers and humid heat.

shoulder.why: Drying out, with festive peak prices.
Rainy season begins with short, heavy showers; Spicemas in August and lower prices.
Showery and humid, but quiet and cheap.

risks.note: Grenada is near the southern edge of the belt, but Ivan (2004) and Beryl (2024) caused severe damage.
Seaweed can reach the south-east and Atlantic-facing bays.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Hotels on Grand Anse are at peak rates; yachts crowd the marinas.

recurringHolidays.name: Spicemas
recurringHolidays.approx: Second Monday and Tuesday of August, with events from late July
recurringHolidays.effect: Grenada's carnival, with J'ouvert 'jab jab' revellers; flights and hotels fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Carriacou Regatta
recurringHolidays.effect: Sailing races and festivities in Hillsborough.

prices.notes: Good value for the eastern Caribbean. Cheap local minibuses run from St. George's to Grand Anse and Gouyave; the Osprey ferry goes to Carriacou.

countries.name: Haiti
countries.summary: The UK and US governments advise against all travel to Haiti because of gang violence, kidnapping and repeated closures of Port-au-Prince airport, so check government travel advice before considering a trip. Climatically the best time is the dry season from December to March, with 31 °C days and little rain. There are two rainy peaks (April–May and August–October), and the hurricane season peaks from mid-August to October, when deforested hillsides are prone to floods and landslides. Kanaval before Lent and the Fèt Gede in early November are the main cultural events.
countries.splitReason: The country is small and shares one Caribbean wet-and-dry calendar; the mountains above Port-au-Prince are cooler but follow the same seasons.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Port-au-Prince and Pétion-Ville, Cap-Haïtien and the Citadelle Laferrière, Labadee, Jacmel, Île-à-Vache and the south coast.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 30–31 °C days, low rainfall and the Kanaval season.

worst.why: Hurricane peak and heavy rain, with floods and landslides on deforested slopes.

shoulder.why: The first rainy season peaks in May with afternoon storms.
A drier, very hot spell (35 °C in Port-au-Prince) as the hurricane season starts.
Rains easing, with the Fèt Gede festival.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; storms cause deadly floods.
Heavy rain triggers floods and landslides in the hills and on the roads.
Port-au-Prince regularly reaches 35 °C.

recurringHolidays.name: Kanaval (Carnival)
recurringHolidays.approx: The three days before Ash Wednesday
recurringHolidays.effect: Haiti's national carnival with rara bands; Jacmel's papier-mâché carnival is held in the weeks before.

recurringHolidays.name: Fèt Gede
recurringHolidays.effect: The Vodou festival of the ancestors fills cemeteries with ceremonies.

prices.notes: Tourism infrastructure is very limited and secure transport is expensive. Most foreign visitors are on organised or NGO-supported trips.

countries.name: Jamaica
countries.summary: Jamaica's dry, sunny season runs from mid-December to April, with 30 °C days and the highest prices, especially over Christmas and New Year. May and October are the wettest months, and the hurricane season (June to November) peaks from mid-August to October; Hurricane Melissa struck the west of the island in October 2025. Summer is hot and showery but cheaper, and late July brings Reggae Sumfest to Montego Bay. The Blue Mountains are cooler and wetter than the coast.
countries.splitReason: The resort coasts share one Caribbean calendar; only the Blue Mountains are noticeably cooler and wetter.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Montego Bay, Negril, Ocho Rios and Runaway Bay, Kingston and the Blue Mountains, Port Antonio and Treasure Beach on the south coast.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 29–30 °C days, low humidity and calm seas on the north and west coasts.

worst.why: Hurricane peak and the wettest weeks (October), with storms, flooding and many hotels closing for refurbishment.

shoulder.why: Warm and good value, but May brings the spring rains and sargassum can reach some beaches.
Hot and humid with afternoon showers; Reggae Sumfest and summer family crowds.
Rain easing and pre-Christmas prices, with lush green hills.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Hurricane Melissa (October 2025) devastated western Jamaica.
The spring rains bring short, heavy downpours.
Seaweed can reach some east- and south-facing beaches.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak rates at the resorts of Montego Bay, Negril and Ocho Rios; book months ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: Rebel Salute
recurringHolidays.effect: A roots-reggae festival on the north coast; nearby hotels fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Jamaica Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Soca fetes and the road march in Kingston; hotels in New Kingston book out.

recurringHolidays.name: Reggae Sumfest
recurringHolidays.effect: The biggest reggae festival in the Caribbean fills Montego Bay; prices rise.

prices.notes: Most visitors stay all-inclusive ($250–500 a night for two). Guesthouses in Treasure Beach and Port Antonio cost $70–150. Check that hotels in the west have fully reopened after Hurricane Melissa.

countries.name: Puerto Rico
aliases: Estado Libre Asociado de Puerto Rico
countries.summary: Puerto Rico, a US territory, is 28–31 °C all year. The drier winter from mid-December to April is the most popular time, with sunshine, a warm sea, big winter surf at Rincón and US snowbird crowds. Rain picks up from May, and the hurricane season (June to November) peaks from mid-August to mid-October; Maria (2017) and Fiona (2022) both hit in September. El Yunque rainforest is wet all year.
countries.splitReason: The island is small and shares one Caribbean calendar; El Yunque is wetter, and the south coast around Ponce is drier.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: San Juan and Old San Juan, El Yunque, Fajardo, Vieques and Culebra, Rincón and the west coast, Ponce and Cabo Rojo.

best.why: Drier, sunny 28 °C days, a warm sea, big surf in Rincón and humpback whales off the west coast (January–March).

worst.why: Hurricane peak: hot, humid and stormy, with a real risk of direct hits and power cuts.

shoulder.why: Dry-season weather but festive peak prices and crowds.
Hotter and more showery, with summer school-holiday crowds; calm seas are good for snorkelling.
The hurricane risk is fading, but the rains continue into November.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to mid-October; Maria (2017) and Fiona (2022) caused island-wide power cuts.
Seaweed can affect east- and south-facing beaches.
Winter swells make north- and west-coast beaches dangerous for swimming.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Puerto Rico's long Christmas season (to Three Kings' Day) and US holidaymakers push up hotel prices.

recurringHolidays.name: Fiestas de la Calle San Sebastián
recurringHolidays.effect: A huge street festival in Old San Juan; streets are packed and parking impossible.

recurringHolidays.name: Semana Santa
recurringHolidays.effect: Puerto Ricans head to the beaches, Vieques and Culebra; ferries sell out.

prices.notes: Prices are in US dollars and US citizens need no passport. Paradores and guesthouses outside San Juan are cheaper; Vieques and Culebra ferries need booking ahead.

countries.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
aliases: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis
countries.summary: Saint Kitts and Nevis are two small volcanic islands at 28–31 °C all year. The dry season from January to April is the best time, with sunshine and calm seas. Late June brings the St Kitts Music Festival, and the shoulder months of May to July are good value. The hurricane season peaks from mid-August to October, and the festive season is lively with Sugar Mas, the carnival, which peaks on Boxing Day and New Year's Day.
countries.splitReason: Two small islands with one tropical climate; the mountain slopes are wetter than the coasts.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Basseterre, Frigate Bay and the South-East Peninsula, Brimstone Hill and Mount Liamuiga on Saint Kitts, and Charlestown and Pinney's Beach on Nevis.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 28 °C days, calm seas and clear views from Brimstone Hill and Nevis Peak.

worst.why: Hurricane peak and the wettest months, with storms and humid heat.

shoulder.why: Warm and good value, with the Music Festival in June; showers increase.
Rains easing, then Sugar Mas carnival and festive peak prices.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Georges (1998) caused severe damage.
Seaweed can reach the Atlantic coast and the South-East Peninsula.

recurringHolidays.name: Sugar Mas
recurringHolidays.effect: Saint Kitts's carnival; J'ouvert and parades on 26 December and 1–2 January, with peak hotel prices.

recurringHolidays.name: St Kitts Music Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: A three-night festival in Basseterre; hotels and flights fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Culturama
recurringHolidays.effect: Nevis's cultural festival in Charlestown.

prices.notes: Upscale resorts on the South-East Peninsula and Nevis; guesthouses in Basseterre and Frigate Bay are cheaper. The Sea Bridge car ferry and water taxis link the two islands.

countries.name: Saint Lucia
countries.summary: Saint Lucia is a mountainous, green island at 29–31 °C all year. The dry season from mid-December to April is the best time for the beaches and for hiking the Pitons, with peak prices over Christmas and New Year. The rains build from June and peak from August to November, which is also the riskiest part of the hurricane season. May (the Saint Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival) and early summer (Carnival in July) are good-value shoulder months.
countries.splitReason: A small island with one tropical climate; the rainforest interior is wetter than the coasts.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Castries, Rodney Bay and Gros Islet, Marigot Bay, Soufrière and the Pitons, Vieux Fort and the rainforest interior.

best.why: Dry season: sunny 29–30 °C days, clear skies for hiking the Pitons and calm seas for snorkelling.

worst.why: The wettest months and peak hurricane season, with heavy downpours, landslides and some resorts closed.

shoulder.why: Dry weather but festive peak prices.
Warm and good value; the Jazz Festival in May and the first showers in June.
Carnival in July, but showers increase and the hurricane season builds.
Still rainy, but yachts of the ARC rally arrive at Rodney Bay and prices are low.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Tomas (2010) caused severe flooding and landslides.
Heavy rain blocks the winding roads to Soufrière.
Seaweed can affect the Atlantic east coast.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Resorts around Soufrière and Rodney Bay charge peak rates with minimum stays.

recurringHolidays.name: Saint Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: Concerts across the island; Rodney Bay hotels fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Saint Lucia Carnival
recurringHolidays.effect: Fetes and the road parade in Castries; Carnival Monday and Tuesday are public holidays.

prices.notes: Upscale resorts dominate; guesthouses in Rodney Bay and Soufrière cost $80–150. Hewanorra airport is 90 minutes' drive from Rodney Bay.

countries.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
countries.summary: Saint Vincent is a volcanic, rainforested island and the Grenadines a chain of small, drier islands that are among the Caribbean's best sailing grounds. The dry season from January to May brings steady trade winds, sunshine and calm anchorages in the Tobago Cays, with the Bequia Easter Regatta. June to November is wet and humid, and the hurricane season peaks from mid-August to October; Beryl (July 2024) devastated Union Island, Mayreau and Canouan, a reminder that early storms happen. Vincy Mas carnival fills Kingstown in late June and early July.
countries.splitReason: The islands share one trade-wind calendar; Saint Vincent's mountains are wetter than the low, dry Grenadines.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Kingstown and Saint Vincent's volcano and rainforest, Bequia, Mustique, Canouan, Mayreau, the Tobago Cays and Union Island.

best.why: Dry season: steady trade winds for sailing, sunny 29–31 °C days and clear water in the Tobago Cays.

worst.why: Hurricane peak and the wettest months, with heavy rain, rough anchorages and many small resorts closed.

shoulder.why: Dry, but festive peak prices; Nine Mornings in Kingstown.
Showery and humid with Vincy Mas, but the hurricane season has begun (Beryl hit on 1 July 2024).
Rains easing and charter prices low.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October, but Beryl struck the Grenadines as a category 4 storm on 1 July 2024.
Heavy rain causes landslides on Saint Vincent's windward roads.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Mustique and the Grenadines resorts are at peak prices; yacht charters book out.

recurringHolidays.name: Bequia Easter Regatta
recurringHolidays.effect: Yacht racing and parties in Admiralty Bay; Bequia guesthouses fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Vincy Mas
recurringHolidays.effect: Saint Vincent's carnival in Kingstown, ending with Mardi Gras.

recurringHolidays.name: Nine Mornings
recurringHolidays.effect: Pre-dawn street parties and concerts in Kingstown before Christmas.

prices.notes: Ferries link Kingstown, Bequia and the southern Grenadines cheaply; a day-sail to the Tobago Cays costs about $150. Mustique and Canouan are luxury-only.

countries.name: The Bahamas
countries.summary: The Bahamas lie just north of the Tropic of Cancer, so winters are cooler than elsewhere in the Caribbean: December to February brings 25 °C days, cool evenings, a 23 °C sea and occasional cold fronts. March to May is the sweet spot, warm, dry and sunny before the rains, though US spring break fills Nassau in March. June to November is hot, humid and wet, and the hurricane season peaks from mid-August to October (Dorian devastated Abaco and Grand Bahama in 2019). Junkanoo parades on 26 December and 1 January are the highlight of the year.
countries.splitReason: The islands share one subtropical calendar; the southern Out Islands are slightly warmer and drier than Nassau and Grand Bahama.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Nassau, Cable Beach and Paradise Island, Grand Bahama, the Exumas, Eleuthera and Harbour Island, the Abacos, Andros and Bimini.

best.why: Warm 27–29 °C days, dry and sunny, with the sea warming to 25 °C before the rainy season and hurricanes.

worst.why: Hurricane peak, with heavy rain and humid heat; many Out Island resorts close in September–October.

shoulder.why: Dry and pleasant but cooler (25 °C) with a 23 °C sea and occasional windy cold fronts; Junkanoo and spring break push up prices.
Hot, humid and showery; cheaper, but the hurricane season has begun.
Rain easing, warm sea and low prices before the winter season.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Dorian (2019) devastated Abaco and Grand Bahama.
Winter cold fronts bring cool, blustery days and rough crossings.
Seaweed can reach east-facing beaches in the southern islands.

recurringHolidays.name: Junkanoo
recurringHolidays.effect: All-night costumed parades on Bay Street in Nassau; hotels are at peak prices.

recurringHolidays.name: US spring break
recurringHolidays.effect: College students fill Nassau and Paradise Island; rates rise.

prices.notes: One of the most expensive Caribbean destinations, as almost everything is imported. Local mailboats and inter-island flights connect the Out Islands; book small guesthouses early for March–April.

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.summary: Trinidad and Tobago lie just off Venezuela, south of the main hurricane belt, and are 31–32 °C all year. The dry season from January to May is the best time, and Carnival in Port of Spain (the Monday and Tuesday before Ash Wednesday) is one of the world's great street parties. The rainy season runs from June to December, with heavy afternoon downpours and flash floods, broken by a short drier spell in September–October. Leatherback turtles nest on Trinidad's north coast and in Tobago from March to August.
countries.splitReason: Both islands share one wet-and-dry tropical calendar; Tobago is a little drier and breezier than Trinidad.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Port of Spain, Maracas Bay and the north coast, the Northern Range and Asa Wright, Caroni Swamp, and Tobago (Crown Point, Castara, Speyside).

best.why: Dry season: sunny 31 °C days, Carnival in Port of Spain and leatherback turtles nesting from March.

worst.why: The wettest months: daily downpours, flash floods in Port of Spain and sticky humidity.

shoulder.why: The rains begin, but turtle-nesting season peaks.
Showery, with a drier spell in September–October; Divali lights and parang music at Christmas.

risks.note: Trinidad is south of the main hurricane belt, but Tobago is occasionally brushed by tropical storms.
Flash floods in Port of Spain and the low-lying east during heavy downpours.

recurringHolidays.name: Carnival
recurringHolidays.approx: The Monday and Tuesday before Ash Wednesday
recurringHolidays.effect: Port of Spain's Carnival: fetes for weeks before, and flights and hotels sell out at triple prices.

recurringHolidays.name: Divali
recurringHolidays.effect: Lights and festivities across Trinidad; a public holiday.

recurringHolidays.name: Tobago Heritage Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: Traditional music, dance and food in Tobago's villages.

prices.notes: Carnival week costs two to three times the usual rates, and costumes with a mas band cost $500–1,500. Tobago guesthouses are good value the rest of the year.

countries.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
countries.summary: The Turks and Caicos are low, dry islands with little rain, famous for Grace Bay's beach and a huge barrier reef. The best time is January to May: sunny 27–30 °C days, low rainfall and humpback whales passing Grand Turk and Salt Cay from January to April. Prices peak over Christmas, US Thanksgiving and spring break. The hurricane season peaks from mid-August to October, when many resorts close, and Irma and Maria both hit in September 2017.
countries.splitReason: Low, flat islands with one dry tropical climate.

regions.name: Whole country
regions.description: Providenciales and Grace Bay, Grand Turk, Salt Cay, North and Middle Caicos, Parrot Cay and South Caicos.

best.why: Dry, sunny 27–30 °C days, calm turquoise water and humpback whales off Grand Turk and Salt Cay (January–April).

worst.why: Hurricane peak, the wettest months and hot, humid air; many resorts close in September.

shoulder.why: Festive peak prices, with occasional cool, windy fronts.
Hot and calm; the hurricane season has begun but prices drop.
Quiet and warm before the Thanksgiving rush.

risks.note: Peak risk mid-August to October; Irma and Maria both hit in September 2017.
Seaweed can reach east- and south-facing beaches, though Grace Bay is sheltered.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Grace Bay resorts at peak rates with minimum stays.

recurringHolidays.name: US Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: American holidaymakers fill Grace Bay; prices jump.

recurringHolidays.name: Conch Festival
recurringHolidays.effect: A food festival at Blue Hills, Providenciales.

prices.notes: Very expensive, with prices in US dollars. Condos with kitchens and the smaller islands (Grand Turk, North Caicos) are better value than Grace Bay's resorts.

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: The USA spans Arctic tundra, subtropical Florida, desert canyon country and Pacific rainforest, so there's no single best season. A rough rule: the south and the deserts are best from autumn to spring, while the north, the mountains and Alaska are summer destinations. Hurricane season (June–November, peaking mid-August to mid-October) affects the Gulf, Florida and the south-east. Wildfire smoke now regularly affects the West from July to October. Thanksgiving, Christmas and the July 4 and spring-break weeks push domestic prices up nationwide.

regions.name: Northeast & New England
regions.description: New York, Boston, Washington DC, Philadelphia and New England (Maine, Vermont, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island).

best.why: A spring of 20–26 °C, with Central Park and the Boston Public Garden in bloom and Broadway and the museums in full swing before the sticky summer humidity.
Crisp, sunny autumn. Peak fall foliage sweeps New England from late September to mid-October, with harvest fairs and comfortable city walking.

worst.why: The coldest stretch (−5 to 5 °C): nor'easter blizzards cancel flights and slush fills the streets. New England ski resorts are the exception.

shoulder.why: Cool and changeable. DC's cherry blossoms (late Mar–early Apr) are a highlight, and hotels are cheaper.
Hot, humid cities (30 °C+ with storms), but it's peak beach season on Cape Cod, Maine and the Hamptons.
Chilly, with Thanksgiving and festive lights. It's magical in NYC, but December hotel prices are among the year's highest.

risks.note: Nor'easters can shut airports and roads for 1–2 days.
Heat waves of 35 °C with high humidity in NYC, Philadelphia and DC.
Direct hits are rare, but the remnants of tropical storms bring flooding.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: The busiest travel days of the year: airfares peak and the Macy's Parade fills Manhattan.

recurringHolidays.name: Holiday season in NYC
recurringHolidays.effect: The Rockefeller tree, windows and Times Square NYE: Manhattan hotels at their annual peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Independence Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Beach towns are full and road traffic is heavy.

recurringHolidays.name: Memorial Day weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: Summer kick-off: Cape Cod and the Hamptons fill.

prices.notes: Manhattan hotels are the priciest in the region (NYC adds about 15% in hotel taxes). New England inns peak in foliage season and need booking months ahead.

regions.name: South & Gulf Coast
regions.description: Georgia, the Carolinas, Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana and Texas: Atlanta, Charleston, Savannah, Nashville, New Orleans, Austin, Houston, San Antonio and the Great Smoky Mountains.

best.why: Azaleas and magnolias at 22–28 °C, before the heavy humidity. It's festival season, with Jazz Fest, Charleston's food festivals and SXSW in Austin.
Dry, sunny and comfortable once the hurricane peak has passed: fall colour in the Smokies and festivals and football weekends across the South.

worst.why: Oppressive heat and humidity (heat index 40 °C+), daily thunderstorms and the peak hurricane threat on the Gulf and Atlantic coasts from late August.

shoulder.why: A mild (10–18 °C), cheap winter with occasional cold snaps. Mardi Gras (Feb/Mar) takes over New Orleans.
Hot and getting humid; Gulf beaches are lively. Hurricane season begins on June 1.
Still warm and humid, with hurricane risk lingering, but prices are dropping.

risks.note: Peak risk is Aug 20 – Oct 10 on the Gulf Coast (Louisiana, Texas, Alabama) and the Carolinas. Get flexible bookings.
Heat index above 40 °C in Texas and Louisiana; heat advisories are common.
'Dixie Alley' tornado season across Alabama, Mississippi and Tennessee.

recurringHolidays.name: Mardi Gras
recurringHolidays.approx: 2 weeks before Lent, moves each year
recurringHolidays.effect: New Orleans hotels triple in price, with 4–5 night minimums.

recurringHolidays.name: Spring Break
recurringHolidays.effect: Gulf and Atlantic beach towns fill with students and families.

recurringHolidays.name: New Orleans Jazz Fest
recurringHolidays.approx: Last weekend of April – first weekend of May
recurringHolidays.effect: New Orleans hotels near capacity.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak domestic travel and airfares.

prices.notes: Nashville and Austin are now pricey on weekends. New Orleans during Mardi Gras and Jazz Fest can cost three times the usual rate.

regions.name: Florida
regions.description: Miami and Miami Beach, Orlando's theme parks, the Florida Keys, Tampa, the Gulf beaches and the Everglades.

best.why: The dry season brings 24–28 °C, low humidity and sunshine from Miami to Key West. It's the Everglades' wildlife season, and there's no hurricane risk.

worst.why: The peak of hurricane season, 32 °C with stifling humidity and thunderstorms nearly every afternoon. Storm evacuations are possible.

shoulder.why: Hot, humid wet season with afternoon storms but a warm sea and calm water for snorkelling the Keys, plus summer deals (except at Orlando parks).
Hurricane risk fading and humidity dropping; good value before the winter peak.

risks.note: Peak Aug 15 – Oct 15. Monitor the National Hurricane Center and buy travel insurance.
Heat index of 40 °C or more, plus frequent lightning storms in the afternoon.

recurringHolidays.name: Spring Break
recurringHolidays.effect: Panama City Beach, Daytona and Miami Beach overflow; hotel rates peak.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Orlando parks at maximum capacity; Miami at peak rates.

recurringHolidays.name: Art Basel Miami Beach
recurringHolidays.effect: Miami Beach hotels triple in price.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: Theme parks are packed and airfares peak.

prices.notes: Key West is the most expensive part of the state. Many Miami Beach hotels add 'resort fees' of $30–50 a night.

regions.name: Midwest & Great Lakes
regions.description: Chicago, Detroit, Minneapolis, Milwaukee, Michigan's lakeshore, Wisconsin's Door County and the Great Plains.

best.why: Warm, long days and the start of festival season (Chicago Blues Fest), with the lakeshore paths and beaches at their best.
Comfortable 18–25 °C days, fall colour in Michigan and Wisconsin, apple harvests and the Chicago architecture boat tours still running.

worst.why: Bitter cold, with −10 to −20 °C wind chills off the lakes, snowstorms and polar vortex outbreaks; lake resorts are closed.

shoulder.why: An unpredictable spring: sunny one day, snowing the next. Tornado season on the Plains.
Hot and humid but lively: lake beaches, Lollapalooza and summer festivals.
Chilly and increasingly grey; Thanksgiving and holiday markets.

risks.note: Lake-effect snowstorms close roads and ground flights at O'Hare.
Polar vortex outbreaks can bring wind chills of −30 °C.
Tornado watches are common across Illinois, Iowa and the Plains.
Humid heat waves of 35 °C or more.

recurringHolidays.name: Memorial Day weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: Lake resorts open and fill.

recurringHolidays.name: Lollapalooza (Chicago)
recurringHolidays.effect: Downtown Chicago hotel rates double.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak domestic travel.

prices.notes: Big convention weeks in Chicago can double hotel prices, so check the convention calendar.

regions.name: Southwest & Canyon Country
regions.description: Arizona, Nevada, Utah and New Mexico: Las Vegas, Phoenix, the Grand Canyon, Sedona, Monument Valley, Zion, Bryce, Arches, Moab and Santa Fe.

best.why: Ideal for canyon country: 20–28 °C days for Zion, the Grand Canyon, Sedona and Monument Valley, with desert wildflowers and comfortable hiking.
The heat breaks. Clear skies, golden cottonwoods, quieter trails and Santa Fe's chile harvest.

worst.why: Dangerous heat (40–47 °C in Phoenix, Las Vegas and Death Valley) makes midday hiking unsafe. The July–August monsoon adds flash floods in slot canyons.

shoulder.why: A pleasant desert winter (Phoenix about 20 °C), but snow closes the Grand Canyon North Rim and some Bryce roads. It's ski season in Utah.
Getting hot in the low deserts, while the high country (North Rim, Bryce) opens fully.
Still hot, but the monsoon storms are ending and crowds are dropping.

risks.note: Heat kills hikers every summer. Hike at dawn and carry 4 litres of water or more.
Monsoon storms upstream can flood slot canyons (Antelope, The Narrows) without warning.
Pre-monsoon fire season in Arizona and New Mexico forests.

recurringHolidays.name: Spring Break
recurringHolidays.effect: National parks are busiest; Zion shuttle lines are long.

recurringHolidays.name: Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta
recurringHolidays.effect: Albuquerque hotels sell out a year ahead.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: Park lodges full.

prices.notes: Las Vegas prices swing wildly with conventions and weekends. Lodges inside the national parks book out 13 months ahead. An America the Beautiful pass ($80) covers park entry.

regions.name: California
regions.description: Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Big Sur, Napa and Sonoma wine country, Yosemite, Lake Tahoe and the Sierra Nevada.

best.why: California's real summer: the warmest sea, clear skies with no June Gloom, harvest in Napa and Sonoma, and smaller crowds after Labor Day.
Green hills, wildflower superblooms in wet years and Yosemite's waterfalls at peak flow. Mild, sunny weather is ideal for road trips.

worst.why: Peak family-holiday crowds and prices: Yosemite and Big Sur gridlocked, the coast often foggy (June Gloom, SF's summer fog) and 38 °C or more inland.

shoulder.why: Mild winter, with storms bringing rain to the coast and snow to the Sierra. It's ski season at Tahoe and Mammoth and grey-whale migration along the coast.
'May Gray / June Gloom' marine layer on the coast while inland heats up; crowds build.
Families heading home, but still busy and hot inland.

risks.note: Fire season peaks Sep–Nov with Santa Ana and Diablo winds; smoke and road closures possible.
Atmospheric-river storms cause mudslides and close Highway 1 at Big Sur.
Death Valley, Palm Springs and the Central Valley often exceed 40 °C.

recurringHolidays.name: Coachella
recurringHolidays.effect: Palm Springs area sold out.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak domestic travel; Tahoe opens.

recurringHolidays.name: Independence Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Beaches and national parks packed.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Ski resorts and Disneyland at peak prices.

prices.notes: San Francisco and Napa are the most expensive; inland and desert towns are much cheaper. Yosemite needs park reservations at peak times.

regions.name: Pacific Northwest
regions.description: Washington and Oregon: Seattle, Portland, the Olympic Peninsula, Mount Rainier, the North Cascades, the San Juan Islands and the Oregon coast.

best.why: Dry, sunny and 22–27 °C: Olympic, Mount Rainier and North Cascades trails free of snow, wildflower meadows, and orca season around the San Juan Islands.

worst.why: Grey, drizzly and dark (sunset around 4:20 pm), with constant rain on the coast and snow closing mountain passes. It's good only for skiing.

shoulder.why: Still wet, with late-season skiing and blossom starting in Seattle.
Spring blooms (Skagit tulips in April) and showers. High trails and Rainier's Paradise stay snowy until July.
Fall colour and salmon runs as the rain returns in October.

risks.note: Smoke from regional fires can bring unhealthy air for days at a time.
Atmospheric rivers cause flooding and landslides on the coast and in the Cascades.
North Cascades Highway and high park roads closed by snow.

recurringHolidays.name: Independence Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Campgrounds and ferries booked out.

recurringHolidays.name: Labor Day weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: End-of-summer rush to the parks and islands.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak domestic travel.

prices.notes: Seattle summer prices rise with Alaska cruise departures. San Juan Islands ferries need vehicle reservations in summer.

regions.name: Rocky Mountains
regions.description: Colorado, Wyoming, Montana and Idaho: Denver, Aspen, Vail, Yellowstone, Grand Teton, Glacier National Park and Jackson Hole.

best.why: Yellowstone, Grand Teton, Glacier and Rocky Mountain parks fully open: wildflowers in July, Going-to-the-Sun Road clear and the elk rut in September.
Prime powder in Colorado, Wyoming and Montana after the holiday rush, with deep snow and sunny bluebird days.

worst.why: Mud season: ski lifts closed, high roads (Beartooth, Going-to-the-Sun) still snowbound, many lodges shut and trails muddy.
The off-season gap: park roads closing, no reliable snow for skiing yet, and many services closed.

shoulder.why: The ski season opens. Christmas week is the most expensive of the year.
Spring skiing in sunny, softer snow, with deals.
Snowmelt and roaring waterfalls, but high passes may still be closed.
Golden aspens and crisp nights as services wind down and roads begin to close.

risks.note: Fires and smoke can close park roads and trails.
Backcountry avalanche danger; check the regional avalanche centres.
Most Yellowstone roads close to cars from early November to late April; mountain passes snowbound.
Afternoon lightning on exposed peaks; be off summits by noon.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year ski peak
recurringHolidays.effect: The year's highest lift and lodging prices.

recurringHolidays.name: Presidents' Day weekend
recurringHolidays.effect: The busiest ski weekend after Christmas.

recurringHolidays.name: Independence Day
recurringHolidays.effect: Yellowstone and Grand Teton at peak capacity.

prices.notes: Aspen, Vail and Jackson are among the most expensive ski towns in the world. Buy Epic or Ikon passes early, as walk-up lift tickets cost $250 or more a day.

regions.name: Alaska
regions.description: Anchorage, the Kenai Peninsula, Denali, Fairbanks, Juneau and the Inside Passage.

best.why: Midnight sun (19+ hours of daylight), Denali park bus fully running, bears fishing for salmon, glacier cruises and every road and lodge open.

worst.why: Darkness (5–6 hours of daylight in Anchorage, less in Fairbanks) and −15 °C, with most tours and lodges closed. Good only for aurora hunting.
Break-up season: muddy snowmelt, closed attractions and no aurora as the nights get bright.

shoulder.why: Aurora season with longer days; the Iditarod sled-dog race starts in early March. −10 °C.
Lodges reopening at low prices, though some roads and tours have not yet started.
Fall colour on the tundra and the first auroras, with discounted rates as the season winds down.

risks.note: Fairbanks can drop below −35 °C; winter driving skills are essential.
Interior fires can bring smoke to Fairbanks and Denali.

recurringHolidays.name: Fur Rendezvous & Iditarod start
recurringHolidays.approx: Late February – first Saturday of March
recurringHolidays.effect: Anchorage hotels busy for the winter festival and race start.

recurringHolidays.name: Cruise season
recurringHolidays.effect: Juneau, Ketchikan and Skagway can see 20,000 cruise passengers a day.

prices.notes: Summer car hire and lodges inside Denali book out early. Small-plane glacier landings cost $300–600 per person.

regions.name: Hawaii
regions.description: Oahu (Honolulu, Waikiki, North Shore), Maui, Kauai and the Big Island (Hawai'i Volcanoes, Kona).

best.why: Dry and sunny, with calmer seas on most coasts. It falls between the winter and summer peaks, so prices are better.
The warmest sea, dry leeward coasts and the fewest visitors of the year.

worst.why: Peak holiday season: the year's highest rates and sold-out flights. Big swells close North Shore beaches to swimmers.

shoulder.why: Rainier winter, but humpback whales (Jan–Mar) and big-wave surf on the North Shore.
The summer family peak: hot, with calm south shores and higher prices.
Thanksgiving week is busy and winter rains are increasing.

risks.note: Direct hits are rare, but tropical storms bring flooding and big surf.
Dangerous winter swells on north-facing shores; heed the lifeguards.

recurringHolidays.name: Christmas & New Year
recurringHolidays.effect: Peak rates across the islands.

recurringHolidays.name: Japanese Golden Week
recurringHolidays.effect: Waikiki busy with Japanese visitors.

recurringHolidays.name: Merrie Monarch Festival (Hilo)
recurringHolidays.effect: Hilo hotels sold out for the hula festival.

recurringHolidays.name: Thanksgiving
recurringHolidays.effect: Busy, with higher airfares.

prices.notes: Expect resort fees ($35–50 a night) and an 18% lodging tax. Maui and Kauai cost more than Oahu.
